groups.why: Two clauses in a row, each with its subject only in the verb (second masculine singular), both acts of the LORD addressed. The cup clause is a state and stands outside the run.
groups.category: run of acts of one agent

cant_tell.what: whether 'You prepare a table ...; You anoint my head ...' is a parallel group
cant_tell.why: the same implied subject, but the second clause does not restate the first's roles (table before foes against head with oil)

cant_tell.what: Whether 'my cup overflows' is what the anointing brings about (a result) or a further image of abundance
cant_tell.why: The clause follows after a semicolon with no conjunction and no verb of result, so no result link is recorded.

cant_tell.what: whether 'my cup overflows' (cl2) is a result of the anointing in cl1
cant_tell.why: No conjunction joins them. The image is set beside the anointing with no stated consequence, and the result link needs the act's effect to be stated.
